decisions.summary: The record first: the village-lanes entry rewritten from what was read (brief R1); the drawing page (brief R2) once D2-D4 land
decisions.why: FR-001 and US1 as written; the GM's question is answered from the research before the engine moves.

decisions.summary: A household asks for a corridor first; only where access_corridor finds none may it be reached by passage
decisions.why: FR-002 puts no such condition on the passage, so this narrows when it applies. Implied by the GM's own words, 'if that is what the research bears out, then we should go with it': every Wigmore passage-to-the-road entry the record reads is conditioned on land that 'cannot reach the highway without passing over' another's (or pouch-land); none attests a household with its own access crossing a neighbor's. Purpose test: the GM's purpose is that no unresearched requirement be imposed, and this condition is the research's own, not an added one. Unchanged from the previous record's ruling; the amendment no longer lets it gut the feature, because tight seats (D2-tight) now make the condition arise.

decisions.summary: While the share has room, each standing house of the grown cluster also offers tight seats at the footprints' parting plus 2 px, without the path's strip
decisions.why: This is what the MODE 1 ruling of 2026-10-03 required: the growth's path-strip spacing (grow_gap) was built for a lane to every house and kept the custom's condition from ever arising (research R3: the first build seated no household). Tight seats are the mechanism by which FR-002's 'MUST be able to seat a household reached across a neighbor's dooryard' can actually happen; bounded by D4's share, which FR-002 asks for.

decisions.summary: A tight seat is taken only by passage: a household that finds its own corridor there is refused the seat; ordinary seats keep a path's room
decisions.why: Narrows nothing the request or spec asked for: no household that could be reached across a yard is excluded by it. It keeps lane households on the spacing they have now, which the spec does not ask to change; letting lane households pack tighter would be new behavior the GM did not request. It is D2-order applied at the tight seat (land with its own access is not land the custom covers).

decisions.summary: The reach is the custom's condition: the household's land - the reach its seat was parted by (settled_seat's allotted reach, over every garden layout, carried with its house) - within the parting and PASSAGE_ADJOIN_FT (GUESS: the 2 px parting plus a foot) of the neighbor's footprint, not a walking distance
decisions.why: Still the spec's 'across a neighbor's dooryard' and the record's 'passing over' another's land, read literally: land against land, never open ground. The amendment changes which ground counts as the household's own - the ground the growth actually reserved for it when parting its seat, rather than one layout's box - which is the household's land in the model (no other homestead may stand on it). It narrows nothing asked: research R6 measured the old measure refusing all but one household at 3-36 px back from the parting (observed 2026-10-03), so the change makes FR-002's 'MUST be able to seat' reachable rather than restricting it.

decisions.summary: The walk from one of the household's dooryard doors to the neighbor's threshing yard, wholly on the two households' land, clear of both households' houses, beds, sheds, byres, well pockets and fixtures, of every other placed homestead, the refused-ground grid and reserved wood seats - ROUTED round them on the map's own router (route.search, route.taut); kept clear of later homesteads; not drawn as a lane (GUESS)
decisions.why: FR-002 'never across a house, a garden bed, a shed or a fixture'; US2 'has no lane of its own' and 'the neighbor's yard is not built over'. Every clearance of the previous version is kept; routing replaces the straight leg, which removes a restriction the request never asked for (R6: the straight leg was blocked on 95 of 109 tight-seat layouts and found 3 passages; routed, 16 households on 9 of 13 settlements whose share allowed one, observed 2026-10-03). Staying on the two lands keeps a third household's land for the chain (D3). Within.

decisions.summary: At a tight seat the walk is asked first, then the corridor; both must hold (a walk exists and no corridor of its own), so the verdict is the same
decisions.why: An evaluation order with the identical verdict as D2-order and D2-tight-refusal: no household is seated or refused differently. A construction choice, not a narrowing of what was asked.

decisions.summary: A chain of passages ends at a corridor within PASSAGE_CHAIN = 2 households, a GUESS citing Wigmore's Echigo entry
decisions.why: The spec's edge case and FR-002 delegate any chain limit to the plan as a labeled GUESS citing Echigo; C over both B's plot and A's is two plots, the longest chain read.

decisions.summary: PASSAGE_SHARE_BAND = (0.0, 0.25) rolled per nucleated settlement from the seed, a GUESS; beyond the share a household is seated only with a corridor
decisions.why: FR-002 asks for a share rolled per settlement within a band the record supports or labels as a guess; labeled, its upper bound reasoned from the record's alleys to rear houses (Morse; the Manchu survey). Calibrated liberty, not a strict rule.

decisions.summary: reached_across on the household record; the one reach predicate (checks.unreached_houses) counts a chain ending at a reached household; nothing else of the ways changes

The corridor judged as drawn, as found: tree.admits asks the needle of the tree with its free ends joined as the web's settle will join them (tree.as_joined, settle.settle_joins / law.near_misses), with an exact box prefilter in law.near_misses and law.free_end (same answers); the route searched per garden layout round the household's own parts, kept because it pays (R4); seed 18's regression closed by tree.laid_run / own_clear
decisions.why: FR-004 and SC-003: the seating admits a corridor only in the form the web will draw it, now including the settle's join that research R2 found actually closed feature 314 R12's sliver. The prefilter is a cost measure with identical answers, not a scope change. FR-005 (seed 18), FR-006 and the GM's concern about disregarding optimizations that work: the withdrawn lever retried and kept only on measurement.

decisions.summary: Known bugs listed with owners: D6's defect here; cohort seeds 14, 15, 906, 22, 23 with the Diagram (Inashiro) session; tooling bugs found on the way, fixed here
decisions.why: FR-007 and SC-006, matching 'coordinate with that other session' and 'I do want all known bugs to be fixed'.

decisions.summary: Unit tests of tight seats, passage, chain, share and reach; SC-002 at 15 households seeds 1-16 with meta.passage_share / passage_reached; refusals/abab at 15 and 40 households, the cohort against main, make done, bookends
decisions.why: Enforces FR-002, FR-003, FR-005, FR-006 and SC-002 as written; checks that the requested behavior happens, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: Performance bookends 317-start / 317-end back to back in a worktree at origin/main
decisions.why: Constitution VI procedure; serves FR-006's timing against the base.
